content.thinking:
I'll need to write the entire file carefully in one pass without verification, building a gnome roughly 1.1m tall facing forward. I'm planning the skeleton structure: hips, spine chain, neck, head, jaw, arms with shoulders/elbows/wrists/fingers, legs, and a backpack joint, using robust joint, chain, sweep, and part APIs.

For positioning, I'm working out specific coordinates for each body part—hips around y=0.42-0.44, legs extending down to ankles near y=0.08, torso rising through chest and neck to a large head centered near y=0.92, topped with a hat peaking around y=1.18-1.2. I'm sketching out how the spine and neck chains should be parented and named so the tip joints come out correctly, then moving on to figure out shoulder placement for the arms.

I'm defining the arm chains as world-coordinate point sequences from shoulder to elbow to wrist, keeping the pose neutral with arms slightly out and down, and naming the joints so the wrist becomes the tip. Now I'm setting up the sweep radii for these arm chains.

For legs, I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle joints similarly, then adding boot geometry as box-shaped parts attached to the ankle joint, with a low-poly toe cap and a swept shaft running up from the knee area.

I'll use the last joint in the chain array as the ankle tip for the boots, confirming the hip-knee-ankle joint count works out for the leg chain. For the torso, I'm sweeping along the spine chain from hips to a shorter span higher up, giving the body a bulbous belly shape with wider radii in the middle.

For the clothing layers, I'm sweeping a cream-colored shirt tight to the spine chain, then adding a brown vest as a second, slightly larger sweep over it to create layered depth.

Now I'm planning the skirt/tunic as a lathed shape flared around the hips joint, and starting to define the head geometry as a low-poly sphere positioned and oriented to the head joint's aim direction.

Adding facial features...

Still designing beard spikes...

Now I'm shaping the hat as a tilted cone sweep with a tapering radius path curving backward, capping total figure height around 1.25m, with a separate brim ring and a brown band with brass buckle detail.

I'm adding goggles on the hat: brass cylinder oculars and glowing cyan glass lenses positioned near the brow, oriented forward-up with their axes aligned to a direction vector.

For the arms, I'm sweeping cream sleeves with cuff rods, then building simple low-poly gloves—a palm sphere plus thumb and finger capsules—keeping joint counts modest with one segment per digit to stay within budget.

Positioning the hand joints and finger chains with tapered radii, then placing the wrist and fingers relative to the arm. Now I'm sketching the backpack structure as a separate joint off the chest, with a boxy trunk shape for the body.

Adding backpack details like a leather grain texture, a brass boiler sphere, a chimney, and a gear made from an extruded toothed outline...

For the clock, I'll place a backward-facing plane with the SVG texture and a brass rim cylinder behind the pack. Then I'm positioning a lantern on the side with a brass cylinder base, glowing orange glass box, and cone top, plus starting a cyan glow cylinder for a flask.

Next I'm adding a scroll shape and laying a horizontal bedroll cylinder across the bottom of the pack with cream color and brown strap rings, then starting a spiral sweep for a copper coil using a helper that wraps a thin tube around an axis with set turns, radius, and pitch.

For pipes I'm sweeping a catmull curve from the boiler to the lantern side using a thin copper tube, then building belt pouches as simple brown boxes at the hips, with a front-left tool pouch holding a wrench made from a gray rod handle plus a small torus for the head instead of risking a self-intersecting extruded outline, and I'm sketching a belt as a loop torus around the waist.

I'm working out the torus transform math for the belt, scaling before rotation so the belt sits flat around the torso with slightly flattened depth to match the body's front-back radius at waist height.

I'll adjust the torso radii slightly so the belt sits just outside at roughly 0.152 to 0.166 range, keeping it mostly visible rather than buried. For the buckle I'm placing a small brass box at the front center of the belt, sized to sit just outside the belt surface. Then I'm planning the vest as a sweep along the spine chain starting partway down the torso.

Adding backpack straps as draped sweeps over the shoulder, using path points that follow the torso surface curvature and a drape helper to keep them conforming naturally.

Head joint parents to neck, with the spine chain running hips to chest through two intermediate joints for proper bending. Arms parent to chest, legs to hips, and I'll skip epaulets and shoulder pads for now, moving to defining the torso sweep with its radius function and color.

Still working out the torso and arm geometry...

I'm shaping the boot: a foot box with a toe sphere, a dark sole box sitting at floor level, and a thicker cuff rod with a small brass buckle near the top of the leg. Then I start defining the color palette for skin, nose, cream, beard shading, and hat tones.

Now I'm rounding out the palette with leather, vest, olive, brass, copper, glass, amber, steel, dark, white, blue, and teal, keeping to roughly 25 distinct colors. I'm planning to apply mottled textures to the hat and boots and a grain texture to the vest and pack before moving on to the face.

For the face, I'm skipping decal eyes and building them from simple low-poly geometry instead, positioning the eye whites and pupils symmetrically on the head sphere so they protrude slightly from the front of the face.

Now I'm adding eyebrows as small cream rods, a pink nose sphere, rounded cheek spheres, curled mustache capsules attached to the head bone, and a dark recessed box for the mouth beneath the mustache.

I'm shaping the head as a flat-shaded low-poly sphere, then building spike-shaped ears using a direction and length parameter with smaller pink inner-ear spikes, and placing a ring of cream hair tufts as spikes around the hat's rim.

Each spike needs its bone explicitly set rather than inferred, so I'm attaching options like bone and color consistently across joints. For the hat, I'm sweeping a tapered path through a few catmull points with heptagonal cross-sections, shrinking radius toward a pointed tip, using a painted color for the surface.

Now I'm adjusting the hat's position so the brim clears the head's brow and eyes — shifting the starting point upward and forward slightly, then adding a torus band ring near the base to sit across the forehead properly.

Then I'm sketching the hat's taper path upward, curving it so the tip droops back slightly, bringing the total head-to-tip height to around 1.24, keeping the gnome's proportions in a reasonable range.

Now I'm placing goggles on the hat: positioning the lens cylinder and brass rim near the brow with a cyan glow glass insert, checking that the strap sits along the band and the lens embeds properly at the hat's front curve. Then I work out hand placement, sizing a glove sphere at the wrist end of the arm path.

Mapping out finger chains as leather-textured swept tubes with tapering radii, and a separate thumb chain with its own two-point path and spans, parented to the wrist. I'm making sure the number of named joints matches the spans-plus-tip count for each chain so the sweep geometry generates correctly.

Then I verify the floor placement by checking sole box dimensions so boots rest exactly at y=0, and I'm setting up the skeletal hierarchy -- pack joint off the chest, hips as a root with implicit spine role, and neck/head joints chained off the chest with aim and direction vectors defining their orientation.

Now I'm working out the pelvis geometry, considering a lathed tunic skirt as a simple non-intersecting quad profile, and thinking through how the skirt's vertical offsets map relative to its attachment bone position along the lathe axis.

I'll keep the circular segments at 10 to avoid clipping, and paint the leather brown with a trim color applied below a height threshold for the hem detail.

I'm attaching the hips bone for the lathe, then placing box-shaped pouches near the skirt's outer radius at the hips, with brass studs and a flap. The left front pouch is bigger, holding tools like wrenches and screwdrivers poking out, and I'm calculating the pouch center position and size to align with the skirt's curve at that height.

Now I'm sketching the backpack frame: a main leather-textured box attached to the pack bone, a flap on top, brass rivets along the edges, corner brackets, and straps—keeping part count under budget by mostly using individual box/sphere primitives rather than merging everything.

Next I'm detailing the boiler assembly: a brass sphere body with torus seam bands and rivet domes, a gauge cylinder mounted on the back with an SVG gauge face texture, and planning the chimney as a lathe or stacked cylinders.

Now I'm sketching the chimney structure with a capped cone and brass band, then moving to the lantern on the left side—building it from a brass base cylinder, an amber-glowing glass box, a conical roof, a ring handle, and four thin corner rods. I'm also noting a flask placement on the right side to balance the composition.

Working through the flask's teal glow cylinder, neck, cork, and brass collars cradled in a bracket, then the bedroll positioned across the bottom with straps and darker end caps. I'm also thinking about adding a small horn or telescope shape and an antenna rod topped with a glowing sphere as extra details.

I'm planning small accessories like a wrench made from a rod and torus, plus texture work using SVGs for a clock face with tick marks and hands, and a gauge with a colored arc and needle. I want to add a small gear emblem patch on the character's chest using a plane texture.

Still computing the torso curvature...

Now I'm writing a function to generate gear-tooth outline points by stepping around each tooth at fractional angles with alternating inner and outer radii.

For the second gear, I'm thinking about adding a hub hole and some dark spoke details across the face to make it look mechanical.

Now I'm sorting out which helper functions to actually import to avoid unused-import errors -- picking createBuilder, catmull, spiral, grain, mottle, paint, rng, svg, and glow, while skipping geometry merging to keep rivet counts small and manageable.

I'm working through the TypeScript radius typing for tuple returns, deciding to use `as const` to force a readonly tuple when needed, and considering faceted vs smooth sides for the torso geometry to get a low-poly look.

For the beard, I'm planning to use grain-based paint for color variation and sketching out a seeded RNG to layer multiple rows of beard spikes with varying counts per row.

I'm working out the geometry for each beard spike—angling them across the jaw's front arc, tuning base position, direction, and length so the center spikes hang longer and the whole thing drapes naturally toward the chest without poking too far forward.

Now I'm setting up Spike's cap shape with a low-poly faceted sphere, and planning helper functions to simplify placing each body part with consistent bone, position, and flat-shading options.

I'm confirming the Joint and PartOptions types are correctly exported, then mapping out rotations and directions for cylinders and toruses, plus deciding that side "1" corresponds to the model's left in world space. I'm sketching tools like the wrench using rods and a torus attached to the hips bone, and starting on a clock SVG icon.

Writing SVG code...

I'm checking that a clock placed on the back of the model reads correctly when viewed from behind, since the plane's front face should still render unmirrored from that angle, and noting the head has no texture. I'm wrapping flat-colored parts in a glow helper for emphasis, finalizing the torso's sweep with colored sectors for the shirt stripe, and setting up the arm's sweep function.

Writing boot leg colors...

Now I'm double-checking the whole script for typos before finalizing it.
